changelog: fix+feat: the chart editor was reading the pipeline's own CSVs wrongly, and the PNG it exports is now the report figure rather than a picture of the screen. (1) THE LABEL COLUMN IS NOT ALWAYS THE FIRST ONE. r_tables/alpha_diversity.csv comes from estimate_richness(), which leaves Sample LAST, and nmds_bray.csv puts it third. The parsers took column 0, so the Shannon chart was labelled with the Observed counts - 133, 295, 168, 295 - and the NMDS points were labelled with their own coordinates. Worse than the wrong labels: every lookup keyed on a sample name then missed, which is why hiding a sample worked on the taxonomy tabs and did nothing on Alpha or Beta. The column is now found by header name, with a fallback to the first column whose data is not numeric. (2) ONE SAMPLE, ONE NAME. estimate_richness() hands back make.names() row names, so that file called a sample Bacteria_Pre.R1 while every other file in the same folder called it Bacteria_Pre-R1. Two spellings are two different samples as far as grouping, colour and visibility are concerned. Names are folded to a key and metadata.csv decides the spelling shown. (3) shannon_rarefaction.csv is long format (Sample,Depth,Shannon) and was read as wide, so every x became 0 and the chart drew four flat lines on the origin. Long files are now pivoted. (4) Rarefaction curves plunged to zero at the right edge because rarefaction.csv writes NA past a sample's own depth and NA was read as a real 0 - a curve has to stop where the sample stops, not collapse. The pen now lifts over gaps. (5) drawLines and drawDendro ignored hidden samples outright; the dendrogram now clusters the SUBMATRIX of visible samples, because average linkage merges in the order the distances dictate and a hidden sample changes where the visible ones join. (6) viz_pipeline.R wrote a corrupt asv_summary.csv: Sample and Reads were sorted by read count while n_ASV was computed in the table's original order, then zipped by position, so every sample was reported with another sample's ASV count. In the U2BI-139 run Pre-R2 was shown with Pre-R1's 133 ASVs. Richness is now matched by name, and taken from the right margin whether taxa are rows or columns. The same script now writes Sample first and unmangled in alpha_diversity.csv. (7) SEVERAL GROUPINGS PER JOB. Every non-id column of metadata.csv is offered as a grouping, a picker chooses which one the chart splits by, and new ones can be added - so 'all four' and 'R1 vs R2' live in one job instead of one run each. dada2_pipeline.R already reads every such column, so a re-run draws a figure for each. Saving writes the whole file back, including columns this editor does not understand: the description column the U2BI-139 metadata was prepared with used to be deleted on every save. (8) EXPORT ALL CHARTS AS PNG, one click, sequentially - one tab fetched, shaped, drawn and rasterised before the next starts, because firing them in parallel would have tabs writing over each other's shape and the files would carry each other's data. (9) An 'Alpha by group' chart: bar at the group mean with every sample drawn on it as a dot, metric selectable, and it says when every group holds one sample so a lone value cannot pass for an average. (10) The exported PNG is now a report figure - 1240x780, title, framed panel, axis titles, headed legend that wraps into columns instead of running off the bottom edge - matching the PDFs the pipeline writes. Downloading a PNG used to hand over a 900x470 copy of the screen. (11) Past the eighth taxon the palette used to repeat exactly: at Top 30, taxa 1 and 9 were the SAME colour and the legend could not be read at all. Each pass now shifts hue and lightness, so all 30 swatches differ. The warning changed with it - it no longer claims colours repeat when they do not. Tests: the suite's fixtures were all hand-written and all happened to put the label in column 0, which is exactly why it stayed green through every bug above. It now runs against the real U2Bio-139-v144Genus result folder as well. 422 checks.
